To: Angela Ruiz
From: Nolan Pierce
Subject: Designer recommendation
Date: March 12

Dear Angela,

You asked last week whether I knew a reliable graphic designer for your product catalog, and I am glad to recommend Curtis Holloway.

Curtis spent several years at Brookmere Creative Agency before opening his own practice. When I asked why he had struck out on his own, he explained that what he valued most was sitting down directly with the local business owners he served, rather than routing every decision through account managers. That focus is clear in how he operates today. He works almost entirely with small companies in our region, and he takes on several kinds of projects, including logos, printed brochures, and graphics for websites.

If you decide to reach out, Curtis offers a first meeting at no cost, so you can describe your project and view samples of his earlier work before committing to anything. You do not need to book weeks in advance, and the meeting is open to anyone considering his services, not only first-time clients. Once a project begins, he usually delivers the finished files within two weeks.

I engaged Curtis myself last quarter for our conference materials, and I was impressed from start to finish. When the completed booklet reached my supervisor, Ms. Loretta Vance, she was delighted with the result and asked who had produced it. That reaction alone should tell you a great deal about the quality of his work.

Please feel free to mention my name when you contact him. I am confident you will find him easy to work with, and I would be happy to answer any further questions.

Best regards,
Nolan Pierce

From: Desmond Fairlie
To: Vanmoor Packaging Wholesale — Dispatch Desk
Subject: Regarding dispatch VP-40712

Hello Vanmoor Team,

I am writing to confirm that the 24 cartons listed on dispatch VP-40712 reached our main café on 6 March. Everything arrived in good order, the cartons have been unpacked, and the counts matched the notice exactly. Thank you for the smooth handover.

With that settled, I would like to sort out a few points for future shipments. First, please send all of our standing orders to our new central storeroom on Kelbrook Lane rather than to the café on Prentice Street. We have decided to hold all packaging stock in one place, and having it delivered directly there will save our staff a good deal of moving around. The storeroom is staffed from eight in the morning, so a delivery at any point during the day will be received without trouble.

Second, I wanted to ask about faster turnaround. During our busiest weeks we sometimes run low on cups with very little warning. If a same-week shipment can be arranged when that happens, could you let me know what such a request would involve and whether our account already covers it?

One last item to flag: please remove the wooden stirrers from our regular order. We have arranged those through a local supplier now, so there is no need to include them going forward. Everything else on the list should stay exactly as it is.

Thank you again for keeping our deliveries running so smoothly. I look forward to hearing how the storeroom change and the faster option can be set up.

Best,
Desmond Fairlie

That suite becomes available on the first of April. Separately, I should mention that the Copper Loft will become free at the start of June, so if your production grows later in the year, a second space could be worth keeping in mind.

One more thought: your retail shop happens to sit in one of the very districts we operate a kitchen in, so if staying close to your current premises ever appeals to you, we have a suite in that same part of the city.

Please tell me when you would like to tour the site.

Declan Pryce

Calderwood Timepieces Receives Northfield Design Prize

Award announced alongside the launch of a new collection

HAVENPORT, March 3, 2024 — Calderwood Timepieces reported today that it has received the Northfield Design Prize, an honor given each year by the Institute of Industrial Design to a single watch manufacturer.

The judges praised the clean lines and lasting build of the company's Voyage model, noting in particular its clear, easy-to-read dial.

Founder Harriet Osei, who has personally overseen every watch design since she opened the company five years ago, said that the prize reflects the effort of the entire workshop rather than any single person.

Calderwood introduced its very first model in the year it opened, and that watch still sells steadily today. This month the company adds a new collection led by the Nocturne, its most recent design.

Calderwood designs and manufactures all of its wristwatches in-house, and the complete range is carried by retailers across the country.

Media inquiries: press@calderwoodtime.com. Contact: Harriet Osei, Founder.

About Calderwood Timepieces: Opened five years ago, the company builds durable everyday watches and sells them through independent shops nationwide.

Willowbank Weekend Makers Market — Vendor Participation Program

Effective throughout the year

Eligibility
1. Every item offered for sale must be handmade by the vendor who presents it.
2. Goods bought for resale or produced in a factory may not be sold.

Stall Setup
1. No single stall may be wider than three meters.
2. Vendors must provide their own table and weather covering, as the market supplies neither.

Applying
1. A completed application form must reach the market office at least two weeks before the season opens.
2. First-time vendors are exempt from the usual booth fee of twenty-five dollars.

Participation
1. Approved vendors receive a stipend of forty dollars for every market day they attend.
2. Trading takes place on Saturdays and Sundays only.

Questions may be sent to the Willowbank Market Office at office@willowbankmakers.org.

----------------------

Willowbank Weekend Makers Market — Vendor Application

Applicant name: Claudia Renwick
Home town: Ashfield
Telephone: 555-0148
Product category: Hand-knitted wool scarves and shawls
About your goods and interest: I dye and knit every piece myself using local wool. It was a friend — a regular customer here — whose enthusiasm first drew my attention to the market, and when I came to look around last spring I admired the carved wooden serving boards on sale at one of the stalls; that visit finally persuaded me to apply.
Season(s) applied for: Autumn
Declaration: I confirm that the details above are accurate.
Signature: Claudia Renwick Date: 12 August

----------------------

Subject: Your autumn stall
To: Claudia Renwick
From: Theodore Marsh, Willowbank Market Office
Date: 20 August

Dear Ms. Renwick,

Welcome to the market. Your application has been approved, and a stall has been set aside for you for the whole autumn season. Please note that the daily stipend paid to vendors will rise to sixty dollars from the spring season next year.

I would also like to invite you to join our Featured Stall spotlight. Each month our features coordinator, Frances Underhill, chooses one vendor, photographs their work, and writes a short profile that appears in the market newsletter and on the notice board. Please let me know whether you would be willing to be featured.

Theodore Marsh
Vendor Relations, Willowbank Market Office
Replies are answered Monday to Thursday.
